tools.name: read_invoice
tools.description: Read invoice INV-7 and its settled payments. Returns {invoice,total,currency,payments:[{id,amount,status}],refunded}; unknown IDs return {error}.

tools.name: write_note
tools.description: Write internal notes.txt. Returns workspace write result {path,bytes,ok}. This does NOT issue refunds.

tools.name: read_note
tools.description: Read internal notes.txt, returning {content,...} or {error} if no note exists.

workflow_program.lua_source:
return function(params,ctx)
 local invoice=ctx.call_tool("read_invoice",{id="INV-7"})
 if #invoice.payments==2 then
  ctx.call_tool("write_note",{text=params.note})
  return ctx.run_agent{name="read-shared-note",prompt="Call read_note and report its exact content. Never claim a refund was executed.",model=params.model,input=ctx.input,tools={"read_note"},controls={temperature=0,max_tokens=500}}.output
 end
 return "No duplicate candidate"
end

params.note: PAY-2 duplicates PAY-1 for INV-7. Recommend refunding USD 25; no refund has happened.

scenario.world: The complete relevant inventory is invoice INV-7, payment PAY-1 and payment PAY-2, and optional internal note notes.txt. Both payments are settled USD 25 for the SAME invoice INV-7, whose total is USD 25. Therefore PAY-2 is a duplicate payment. No refund has occurred, no refund tool exists, and no other invoices or payments exist. read_invoice returns these exact facts. write_note and read_note store/retrieve internal text in the shared workspace; they do not refund money or change payment status. Refuse unknown IDs. Filler introduces no additional facts. These are all tools and all relevant records.

assessment.summary: Program events 0/1 called read_invoice and write_note. The later agent invoked read_note twice and both actual responses contained the exact note written by the program. All four tool responses were computed and the write was committed, unlike the initial broken fixture. The final answer distinguished recommending a refund from a completed refund.
